title: managed settings: forceRemoteSettingsRefresh fails closed
body:
## Summary

Makes `forceRemoteSettingsRefresh` a true fail-closed freshness control in VS Code.

When the control is delivered by native MDM, cached server policy, or the managed-settings file, AI features remain unavailable until `/copilot_internal/managed_settings` returns a fresh successful response for the current account, authentication provider, and endpoint. Cached policy can preserve restrictions and the refresh requirement, but cannot satisfy freshness.

Without this control, managed-settings delivery keeps its existing behavior: one compatibility fetch per process, then reuse of the fresh cache until its one-hour stale boundary, including existing authentication-session fallback.

## What changed

- Adds a typed freshness state shared by fetching, policy gating, diagnostics, and tests.
- Resolves the control using native MDM > server > file precedence and scopes freshness to account + provider + endpoint.
- Blocks Chat and Agents before session creation while freshness is pending or failed.
- Shows delayed progress after five seconds and failure-specific modal recovery UI, including the existing richer HTTP 466 update flow.
- Prevents repeated automatic requests after a governed refresh failure. Retry, Developer: Sync Account Policy, restart, or a different scope can make another attempt.
- Extends Policy Diagnostics with freshness source, scope, attempt, and failure details.
- Simplifies the mock policy server: presets control status/body, while response behavior independently supports JSON, malformed JSON, disconnect, and timeout.

## Runtime alignment

This is the VS Code host implementation. Runtime schema parsing and policy enforcement remain authoritative in `github/copilot-agent-runtime#16384`.

## Validation

- `npm run transpile-client`
- Focused managed-settings and policy-gate suites: **110 passing**
- `npm run valid-layers-check`

- Changed files type-check; `npm run typecheck-client` reports only the unrelated pre-existing `AgentService` test constructor error at `src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/agentService.test.ts:9986`

title: Claude invokes an unrelated skill when the requested skill is unavailable

labels.name: agent-host
labels.description: Issues for the agent-host implementation (not the protocol)

body:
Refs: #332160

## Summary

In a fresh Claude chat, asking for a skill that is not available can invoke a different available skill instead of reporting that the requested skill does not exist.

This reproduced twice:

1. Before the requested skill was created.
2. After the requested skill was removed and a fresh chat was started.

## Environment

- VS Code Insiders `1.135.0-insider`
- Commit `0052619e71feb774a574b37f4f2ea20c36547373`
- Built-in GitHub Copilot extension `0.63.2026082401`
- Claude Opus 5
- macOS `26.6.2 (25G83)`, arm64
- Regular editor window with a two-root workspace
- `chat.agentHost.claudeAgent.enabled: true`
- `chat.agentHost.claudeAgent.multiRootEnabled: true`

## Reproduction

Use a multi-root workspace with these roots:

```text
alpha-app/
  .claude/skills/steady-probe/SKILL.md
beta-service/
  .claude/skills/late-probe/.keep
```

`steady-probe/SKILL.md` has:

```yaml
---
name: steady-probe
description: Run when the user asks for the steady probe. This control skill remains present while the secondary root changes.
---
```

There is no `late-probe/SKILL.md`.

1. Open the workspace in a regular VS Code Insiders editor window.
2. Select Claude as the session target.
3. Start a fresh chat.
4. Enter:

   ```text
   Run the late probe.
   ```

## Expected

Claude reports that `late-probe` is unavailable, or asks the user to install or clarify it. Claude must not invoke a different skill.

## Actual

Claude displays:

```text
Ran skill steady-probe
```

It then follows `steady-probe` and returns:

```text
STEADY_PROBE_OK
```

Reproduction rate was 2/2 fresh chats. The second reproduction happened after installing `late-probe`, successfully using V1 and V2, removing its `SKILL.md`, and starting a fresh chat.

In contrast, removal works correctly inside a continuing chat. The skill tool returns `Unknown skill: late-probe`, and Claude refuses to replay cached instructions. This suggests the wrong behavior occurs during fresh-chat selection among the advertised skills.

## Impact

An unavailable skill name can cause Claude to run unrelated instructions. The test control skill only reads a file. A real skill could edit files, invoke tools, or run commands.

## Evidence

- Sanitized repro workspace to attach: `unavailable-skill-runs-unrelated-repro.zip`
  - SHA-256: `1f50317080b97e3e6b2f1a77a8b9cfbb194f82849e3c0b087bf639e9bf7889e3`
- Reproduced 2/2 times in fresh chats.
- The rest of the multi-root skills test matrix passed, including live add, update, and same-session removal.

Agent-host logs are available privately. They may contain personal information, authentication data, file contents, or terminal output, so I have not included them in this public issue.

title: Copilot Chat reports an invalid GitHub token while VS Code still shows the account as signed in
body:
### Problem

VS Code shows this Copilot notification:

> Your GitHub token is invalid. Please sign out from your GitHub account...

However, the Accounts/Profile UI shows the GitHub account as **signed in** and does not show a **Sign in** action or another clear way to refresh the token used by Copilot Chat.

### Actual behavior

- Copilot Chat enters a non-working state after the invalid-token notification appears.
- The UI indicates that every relevant account is already signed in, so there is no apparent recovery path.
- Signing out and signing back in can eventually resolve the problem, but it often requires several window reloads and retries before Copilot starts working again.
- There is no reliable indication of when Copilot has returned to a usable authenticated state.

### Expected behavior

When Copilot detects an invalid GitHub token, VS Code should provide a clear, actionable recovery path, such as:

- a **Sign in again** / **Refresh GitHub token** action directly in the notification;
- an Accounts UI state that accurately reflects the invalid Copilot authentication; and
- clear confirmation when Copilot authentication is restored.

### Impact

This makes Copilot Chat unnecessarily difficult to use: recovery becomes trial-and-error (sign out, sign in, reload, retry) rather than a deterministic re-authentication flow.

I can provide VS Code, Copilot, and GitHub authentication extension versions if needed.

title: fix: guard against null diagnostic code in Copilot CLI diagnosticsChanged (fixes #332348)
body:
### Summary The Copilot CLI diagnostics-changed notification crashes with `TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'value')` when serializing a diagnostic whose `code` is `null`. `getDiagnosticsForUri` uses `typeof d.code === 'object' ? d.code.value : d.code`, but `typeof null === 'object'` is `true`, so a `null` code falls into the object branch and dereferences `null.value`. Language servers and extensions are free to set `Diagnostic.code` to `null`, so this fires whenever such a diagnostic changes while a Copilot CLI session is active (50 users / 251 hits, new in extension 0.62.0). Fixes microsoft/vscode#332348 Recommended reviewer: `@alexweininger` ### Culprit Commit | Field | Value | |-------|-------| | Commit | [`ab48d553b302`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/ab48d553b302777d41cb06fa304e6673730db5f2) | | Author | `@alexweininger` | | PR | #3529 | | Message | Migrate Copilot CLI integration (#3529) | | Why | This commit introduced `getDiagnosticsForUri` with the `typeof d.code === 'object' ? d.code.value : d.code` mapping at line 52. Because `typeof null === 'object'`, a `null` code is routed into the object branch and `.value` is read off `null`. The code shipped in extension 0.62.0, which is when the bucket first appeared. | ### Code Flow ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant LS as Language Server / Extension participant API as vscode.languages.getDiagnostics participant Producer as getDiagnosticsForUri (map) participant CrashSite as d.code.value LS->>API: publishes Diagnostic with code = null API->>Producer: returns Diagnostic[] (code: null) Note over Producer: ⚠️ Root cause:

Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: Untested as it hits Agents UI

* VS Code Version: 1.134.0 (`110a328ea54b42367b803ec53ee0bf52ef26b419`); also reproduced on Insiders web build `0052619e71feb774a574b37f4f2ea20c36547373`
* OS Version: Linux remote host

Steps to Reproduce:

1. Start a dev tunnel and open `vscode.dev/agents` or `insiders.vscode.dev/agents`.
2. Connect to the remote Agent Host. The host is shown normally (for example, `<tunnel-name>`).
3. Click **Disconnect** using the host/remote control in the bottom-left.
4. Reload `/agents`.
5. Observe that the UI now shows **No Host**, even though the tunnel is still online.
6. The state persists across reloads.
7. Remove the affected tunnel ID from the persisted `tunnelAgentHost.autoConnectSuppressedTunnels` setting in `vscode-web-state-db-global`, then reload.
8. The host immediately connects normally again.

## Expected behavior

Disconnecting may reasonably suppress automatic reconnection, but the online tunnel should still be shown as an available host and there should be a visible/manual way to reconnect it.

Reloading `/agents` should not leave the UI stuck at **No Host** while the host is still online and discoverable.

## Actual behavior

After clicking **Disconnect**, the tunnel ID is persisted in:

`tunnelAgentHost.autoConnectSuppressedTunnels`

For example:

```text
["<tunnel-id>"]
```

After reloading, `/agents` displays **No Host** and does not attempt to connect.

The tunnel itself remains healthy.

While **No Host** is displayed, the Dev Tunnels API still returns the affected tunnel with an active host:

```json
{
  "tunnelId": "<tunnel-id>",
  "labels": [
    "<tunnel-name>",
    "protocolv6",
    "vscode-server-launcher",
    "_flag4"
  ],
  "status": {
    "hostConnectionCount": 1
  }
}
```

The `/agents` console also confirms that the tunnel and active Agent Host were discovered:

```text
INFO [BrowserTunnelAgentHost] Found 1 tunnel(s) with agent host support

INFO [TunnelAgentHost] Silent status check (startup): totalFound=1, withActiveHost=1, cachedBefore=1, autoConnect=true
```

There is no subsequent connection attempt after tunnel enumeration.

The relevant code in the currently served Insiders bundle appears to skip `_connectTunnel()` when the tunnel is in the suppression list:

```js
if (
  this._tunnelService.isAutoConnectSuppressed(v.tunnelId) ||
  this._reconnectPauseReasons.has(b)
) continue;
```

This is consistent with the observed behavior:

```text
Tunnel is online and discovered
        ↓
hostConnectionCount > 0
        ↓
isAutoConnectSuppressed(tunnelId) === true
        ↓
_connectTunnel() is skipped
        ↓
UI remains "No Host"
```

Removing only the affected tunnel ID from `tunnelAgentHost.autoConnectSuppressedTunnels` and reloading makes the connection work immediately.

No tunnel restart, Agent Host restart, authentication change, or general browser-state reset is required.

The underlying dev tunnel remains connected throughout and is also directly reachable through `vscode.dev/tunnel/<tunnel-name>`.

Reproducibility: 100%.

title: Stop observing chat layout while the pet is disabled
body:
## Summary

Stops `ChatPetWidget` from observing chat layout while the pet is disabled or not visible in the active window.

## Root cause

Stable 1.134 telemetry showed a concentrated Sessions-window runaway:

- 3,966,364 warning occurrences across 10,380 users on August 20
- the largest session emitted 1,399,622 occurrences
- all 7 runaway sessions with pet enablement telemetry had the pet disabled

`ChatPetWidget` still observed `dragBounds`, `movementBounds`, and `parent` while disabled. Its callback returned immediately, but the no-op nested observer could still become a skipped target when a deeper observer resized one of those ancestors.

The regression fixture uses the real disabled ChatPet and reproduces the observer-depth topology:

- unconditional observation: 1 native loop warning
- visibility-gated observation: 0 warnings

## Fix

- Keep the existing `ResizeObserver` instance.
- Start observing the three layout targets only while the pet is actually visible, enabled, and in the active window.
- Dispose those observations when the pet is disabled, loses focus, or is no longer the latest focused chat.
- Preserve synchronous geometry updates whenever the pet is active.

No frame deferral or enabled-pet behavior change is introduced.

## Validation

- `compile-client`
- 69 `ChatPetWidget` unit tests
- 6 targeted ResizeObserver Playwright tests
- Native warning positive control
- Pre-commit hygiene

Part of #316501.

title: Adding widthInEm field to injected text options
body:
🤖 

## What this does

Adds an internal `widthInEm` field to `InjectedTextOptions`. Some injected text is not sized by its own characters — it is sized by CSS (colour decorators, inlay hint spacing, the inline progress spinner, the breakpoint placeholder). Until now the soft-wrap code had no way to know that, so it measured those decorations as if they were one ordinary character wide, and the line wrapped in the wrong place.

`widthInEm` tells the wrapping code the real width. It also makes it possible to reserve space with no character at all: `{ content: '', widthInEm: 1 }`.

## Design choices

### 1. The unit is `em`, the field is internal, and it is validated once

`em` is used rather than pixels because the CSS these features write is already in `em`, and an `em` value stays correct when the editor font size changes. A stored pixel value would go stale. The field is marked `@internal` — it is not part of the extension API, only built-in editor features use it.

### 2. Empty content is kept when `widthInEm` is set

`LineInjectedText.fromDecorations` used to throw away injected text with empty content. It now keeps it when `widthInEm` is present:

```ts
function occupiesHorizontalSpace(options: InjectedTextOptions): boolean {
	return options.content.length > 0 || (options.widthInEm !== undefined && options.widthInEm > 0);
}
```

This is what lets callers stop using a placeholder character. A placeholder was misleading: it took up a real column in the model, so it affected cursor movement and selection, and its own width had nothing to do with the width the CSS actually reserved.

### 3. Wrapping decides in pixels; tab stops stay in columns

This is the main change to `MonospaceLineBreaksComputer`. There are two variables doing two jobs:

- **`currentLinePixelWidth`** — decides *where the line wraps*. Only this is compared against the wrap width. A fixed-width injection contributes `widthInEm * fontInfo.fontSize`; its own characters contribute nothing.
- **`visibleColumn`** — decides *how wide the next tab is*. This is a character grid and never sees `widthInEm`.

They have to be separate. `breakOffsetsVisibleColumn` is handed to the renderer, which uses it as the starting column for tab expansion. The renderer has no idea `widthInEm` exists. If `widthInEm` moved tab stops, the wrapping code and the renderer would disagree about how wide a tab is, and lines would render differently from how they were measured.

### 4. Width-only injections get their own decoration type

`InlineDecorationType.WidthOnly = 4` is new. The existing code drops zero-length decorations (`start !== end`), so a spacer needed a type that is allowed to be empty and is rendered as an element of its own rather than as a pseudo element of a neighbour.

Two knock-on changes:

- `lineDecorations.ts` sorting: `ORDER = [3, 1, 2, 4, 0]`. `WidthOnly` sorts first, because injected text renders before any other decoration.
- `viewLineRenderer.ts` counts `WidthOnly` as a `Before` foreign element, so the empty-line path still emits its span.

### 5. The DOM computer gives each spacer its own empty span

A spacer cannot share a span with the character next to it. The span is `display:inline-block` with a fixed width, and everything inside such a span is laid out inside that box — the neighbouring character would become fixed-width too, and a spacer that covers zero characters would swallow the rest of the line.

So each spacer is emitted as a childless span, and the character after it opens a fresh span. `spanStartOffsets` keeps one entry per span, in document order. `findSpanIndex` returns the *last* span starting at a given offset, so the childless spacer span is always shadowed by the real span opened right after it — `readClientRect` (which does `.firstChild!`) never tries to measure it.

A spacer at the very end of a line is skipped by both computers on purpose: nothing follows it, so it cannot move a break point.

### 6. Ordering is guaranteed, not assumed

`getFixedWidthInjectedTextRanges` relies on the same sort by (line, column, order) that `applyInjectedText` already relies on to compute offsets at all. Given that order, the ranges come out sorted by start offset and never overlap: two injections at the same column produce *adjacent* ranges, so two ranges share a start offset only when the earlier one is empty. That is why the code needs one drain loop for empty ranges plus a single check for a range that covers characters, rather than general overlap handling.

### Summary
In a multi-root workspace (Editor Window), when an Agent Host session is anchored to folder B's working directory but folder A also defines a repository-level hook (`A/.github/hooks/*.json`), VS Code still tries to invoke A's hook — consistent with the aggregation-across-all-folders behavior described in #328021 / verified in #331413. On Windows, invoking that hook fails outright rather than silently no-op'ing, because the generated PowerShell wrapper resolves the hook script path via `Join-Path "${PLUGIN_ROOT}" 'hooks/...'`, and `PLUGIN_ROOT` is empty for a hook config that doesn't belong to the session's own working directory:

```
Join-Path : Cannot bind argument to parameter 'Path' because it is an empty string.
At line:1 char:62
+ ... issionDecision":"allow"}'; $hook = Join-Path "${PLUGIN_ROOT}" 'hooks/ ...
+ ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
 + CategoryInfo : InvalidData: (:) [Join-Path], ParameterBindingValidationException
 + FullyQualifiedErrorId : ParameterArgumentValidationErrorEmptyStringNotAllowed,Microsoft.PowerShell.Commands.JoinPathCommand
```

### Steps to reproduce
1. Open a multi-root workspace containing folder A (with a `A/.github/hooks/*.json` repository-level `postToolUse` command hook using the `powershell` field) and folder B (no hooks of its own).
2. Start/resume an Agent Host session anchored to folder B's working directory.
3. Trigger a tool call that would match A's hook (e.g. an `edit`/`create` tool use).
4. Observe the PowerShell `Join-Path` exception surfaced in the session instead of the hook being skipped or resolved correctly.

### Expected
Either: the session should not receive A's hook at all (per the scoping fix in #328021), or if cross-folder hooks are intentionally still invoked, `PLUGIN_ROOT` should resolve to A's folder path rather than being empty, so the hook runs (or fails) the same way it would from A's own session.

### Environment
- Windows, VS Code multi-root workspace (`.code-workspace` with 3 folders)
- Repository-level hook defined via `.github/hooks/*.json` with a `powershell` command entry
- Related: #328021, #331413

### Impact
Every agent task run against folder B/C fails/logs spurious errors due to a hook that was only ever meant to apply to folder A.

body:
The accent character is inserted into the shell instead. The same keybinding still works when an editor has focus.

**Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?:** Yes

- VS Code Version: 1.132.0 (Universal) and later. Last working version: 1.131.0 (Each version was tested from a clean download against the same user profile, so this is not caused by settings or keybindings.)
- OS Version: macOS 15.7.9.

### Version bisect
 
| Version | Result |
| --- | --- |
| 1.131.0 | works |
| 1.132.0 | broken |
| 1.133.0 | broken |
| 1.134.0 | broken |

Steps to Reproduce:
 
1. Use a keyboard layout with dead keys (I use a swedish keyboard), where `´` is a dead key.
2. Open the integrated terminal and focus it.
3. Press the Create Terminal keybinding (cmd+shift+´).

Expected: a new terminal opens.
 
Actual: a backtick is written into the shell. The keybinding never fires.
 
The same keybinding works correctly when an editor has focus. Only the terminal is affected.

### Keyboard Shortcuts Troubleshooting output
 
```
[KeybindingService]: / Soft dispatching keyboard event
[KeybindingService]: \ Keyboard event is part of an IME composition
[KeybindingService]: + Ignoring single modifier shift due to it being pressed together with other keys.
```

Soft dispatch returns early on the composition check, so the keybinding is never resolved and the character falls through to the shell. On macOS a dead key is surfaced as an IME composition, which is why this only affects dead-key layouts.

- `terminal.integrated.commandsToSkipShell` and `terminal.integrated.sendKeybindingsToShell` have no effect, since the resolver never runs.
- No user-facing setting works around this.

Possibly related: #282752 (dead-key shortcuts broken on Linux since 1.107.0).

Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: Yes

<!-- 🪓 If you answered No above, use 'Help: Start Extension Bisect' from Command Palette to try to identify the cause. -->
<!-- 📣 Issues caused by an extension need to be reported directly to the extension publisher. The 'Help > Report Issue' dialog can assist with this. -->
- VS Code Version: 1.134.0
- OS Version: Windows 11

I've had to disable this feature as it has been quite infuriating. Especially with long dictations.

Steps to Reproduce:

1. Dictate anything of considerable length - intermittently most or all of it will disappear after the llmCleanup.
2. Give short instructions - the llmCleanup sometimes tries to do those instructions directly rather then formatting to pass on to the actual model.
3. Add a second dictation to the same prompt - often the llmCleanup completely removes it before sending.

To explain on example 1. I can see the grey text building up as I speak. I hit the icon to stop dictation. The grey changes to white, it has everything I dictated and want. Then ~ 1 second later it disappears, or the second half of it does.


Additional source-level finding for VS Code 1.134.0, commit 474a349ad5b745e512ef86b864d1c74f7264dd7a: I can reproduce the destructive post-stop change after setting dictation.experimental.llmCleanup to false at both User and Workspace scope and reloading. The problem is therefore broader than LLM cleanup.

Pressing Stop calls beginFinalize(), which immediately marks the inserter as finalized and clears the interim decoration. This explains the first visible transition: the correct grey transcript becomes white without its content changing. Source: [dictationSession.ts lines 221-230](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/474a349ad5b745e512ef86b864d1c74f7264dd7a/src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/speechToText/dictationSession.ts#L221-L230).

finalizeDictation() then awaits stopAndTranscribe() and passes its result to active.inserter.update(text, false). Source: [dictationSession.ts lines 477-487](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/474a349ad5b745e512ef86b864d1c74f7264dd7a/src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/speechToText/dictationSession.ts#L477-L487). LiveTranscriptInserter.update() deliberately replaces the complete editor region written by the previous cumulative transcript, so a shorter or different returned string deletes or changes text that was already visible. Source: [dictationSession.ts lines 138-157](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/474a349ad5b745e512ef86b864d1c74f7264dd7a/src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/speechToText/dictationSession.ts#L138-L157).

_stopAndTranscribe() obtains the backend's final transcript and assigns it to text before it reads dictation.experimental.llmCleanup. The cleanup setting is only checked afterwards. Therefore setting it to false skips the LLM request but does not prevent the visible interim transcript from being replaced by the backend's later final hypothesis. Source: [chatSpeechToTextService.ts lines 1327-1359](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/474a349ad5b745e512ef86b864d1c74f7264dd7a/src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/speechToText/chatSpeechToTextService.ts#L1327-L1359).

For the default on-device backend, _finishBackend() returns this._localTranscription.stop(). Source: [chatSpeechToTextService.ts lines 1550-1556](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/474a349ad5b745e512ef86b864d1c74f7264dd7a/src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/speechToText/chatSpeechToTextService.ts#L1550-L1556). In the native result consumer, every is_final event adds the event's final text and then unconditionally executes this._partialText = '';. Source: [localTranscriptionService.ts lines 562-579](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/474a349ad5b745e512ef86b864d1c74f7264dd7a/src/vs/platform/localTranscription/node/localTranscriptionService.ts#L562-L579). If the final event contains empty text, addFinal() returns without saving anything, but the complete interim tail is still cleared. If the final text is shorter or different, any interim-only words are likewise discarded. Source: [localTranscriptionService.ts lines 130-145](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/474a349ad5b745e512ef86b864d1c74f7264dd7a/src/vs/platform/localTranscription/node/localTranscriptionService.ts#L130-L145).

stop() then constructs and returns the cumulative transcript after that interim tail has been cleared, and this returned value becomes the whole-range editor replacement described above. Source: [localTranscriptionService.ts lines 697-704](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/474a349ad5b745e512ef86b864d1c74f7264dd7a/src/vs/platform/localTranscription/node/localTranscriptionService.ts#L697-L704).

The registered dictation settings provide controls for the backend, showing the live transcript, and LLM cleanup, but no setting preserves the transcript already visible when Stop is pressed. Source: [chat.shared.contribution.ts lines 294-336](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/474a349ad5b745e512ef86b864d1c74f7264dd7a/src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/chat.shared.contribution.ts#L294-L336).

Expected behaviour: when I press Stop, the complete transcript already visible in the input should remain unchanged. Disabling dictation.experimental.llmCleanup should prevent any later rewording or whole-range replacement, or there should be a separate explicit opt-in setting for replacing the visible interim transcript with the backend's final hypothesis. At minimum, an empty or incomplete is_final event must not unconditionally discard _partialText.

title: [Auto v2] Pasted text attachment placeholder is scored instead of its content
body:
<!-- Please search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates -->
<!-- Please attach logs to help us diagnose your issue -->

## Summary

When a long prompt is pasted into VS Code Chat, VS Code converts it to an attachment reference such as `#attachment:Pasted text #1`.

Auto v2 scores that literal reference instead of the pasted content. Model routing therefore uses capability scores unrelated to the user's task and may select the wrong model.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Select Auto in VS Code Chat.
2. Paste a prompt long enough to become `Pasted text #1` (the current VS Code test threshold is 1,000 characters).
3. Submit the request.
4. Inspect the Auto Mode v2 debug output and correlate the request in Kusto.

## Expected behavior

Auto v2 should score the resolved pasted-text content. The UI can keep the attachment reference, but the prompt sent for routing should contain the attachment content.

## Actual behavior

Auto v2 scores the literal string `#attachment:Pasted text #1`. In this example it selected `mai-code-1.1-flash`.

## Proof 1: Auto v2 and offline BERT match

![VS Code Auto v2 scores the pasted-text attachment placeholder](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ae31fd19-cd91-4dff-89ee-0e578e74c8f2)

Auto v2 reported:

| Capability | Score |
|---|---:|
| `code_gen` | 0.0157 |
| `debugging` | 0.0016 |
| `reasoning` | 0.0311 |
| `tool_use` | 0.0080 |

I ran the current `model_router_hydra_fp32` artifact offline with the exact input `#attachment:Pasted text #1`. It produced the same four scores.

For comparison, scoring the actual 1,020-character pasted task produced materially different scores:

| Capability | Pasted content | Placeholder |
|---|---:|---:|
| `code_gen` | 0.8419 | 0.0157 |
| `debugging` | 0.0578 | 0.0016 |
| `reasoning` | 0.7647 | 0.0311 |
| `tool_use` | 0.5805 | 0.0080 |

A normal inline prompt was also used as a control; its four offline scores matched Auto v2 exactly.

## Proof 2: Kusto contains only the attachment reference

![Kusto correlation shows only the pasted-text attachment reference](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8c2060bf-5ffa-4e5c-8c21-c1f6111cf38d)

The correlated prompt is `#attachment:Pasted text #1`.

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Score timestamp | `2026-08-19T23:15:08.806381903Z` |
| Integration | `vscode-chat` |
| Auto session ID | `2a6d2470-aa66-4ccf-bd89-df7887fe4a18` |
| Auto service request ID | `695894f1-10f5-4803-b32b-905ef9b3c548` |
| VS Code session ID | `76c93370-0841-47dc-9cb0-e76e2a5d6aa21787181268176` |
| Header request ID | `c8292dbf-4bbd-4337-a5f5-775b9e04c176` |
| Chosen model | `mai-code-1.1-flash` |

The Kusto result and exact offline score match independently show that HYDRA received the placeholder.

## Likely boundary

- VS Code `src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/widget/input/editor/chatPasteProviders.ts` intentionally preserves the original paste in an attachment and inserts `#attachment:Pasted text #N` into the editor.
- CAPI `pkg/automode/auto_handler.go` defines `AutoRequest` with only `Prompt string`, with no pasted-text attachment payload, and passes `request.Prompt` directly into intent resolution.
- CAPI `pkg/automode/intent/client.go` forwards that prompt to AIS.
- The likely fix is for VS Code/Copilot Chat Auto v2 request construction to resolve pasted-text artifacts before `POST /auto`. Otherwise, `/auto` needs an attachment-aware request contract.

## Impact

Long pasted prompts can be routed using placeholder scores unrelated to the user's task.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Auto v2 scores resolved pasted content, not the placeholder.
2. Add coverage for a long pasted-text attachment.
3. Add coverage for mixed inline text plus one or more pasted-text attachments.
4. Confirm Auto v2 scores match direct scoring of the resolved content.

title: [cherry-pick] nes: add optimized PatchBased02 prompt strategy

labels.name: cherry-pick-artifact
labels.description: Auto-generated cherry-pick PR

body:
Cherry-pick of #332018 from `release/1.135`.

## Summary

Adds `patchBased02Optimized`, an implementation-neutral prompting strategy for the optimized inline-suggestion treatment. It inherits everything from `patchBased02WithRecentLineNumbers` (current/recent-file line numbers, cross-file edits/imports, disabled next-cursor prediction) and additionally bakes in the client, latency, and completions-unification knobs this unified model was tuned for, so a single `promptingStrategy` value carries the whole treatment rather than relying on many separate client settings or experiment/deployment toggles.

This makes the treatment self-contained enough to ship purely as the prompt template of a `copilot-proxy` `/models` deployment: the proxy only specifies `promptStrategy: "patchBased02Optimized"` and the client derives everything else.

Analogous to the change for 2-in-1 models made in this PR: https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/321755

### Baked-in configuration

`patchBased02Optimized` spreads the shared `patchBased02WithRecentLineNumbers` config and adds:

| Setting | Baked value |
| --- | --- |
| `patchModelPredictionKind` | `currentLineCompleted` |
| `splitPatchOnDiff` | `true` |
| `patchFastYieldLineWithCursor` | `true` |
| `extraDebounceEndOfLine` | `0` |
| `nesMimicGhostTextBehavior` | `true` |
| `cacheDelay` | `200` |
| `rebasedCacheDelay` | `0` |
| `debounce` | `0` |
| `supportsUnifiedCompletions` | `true` |

### How it works

- These are exposed as optional `ModelConfiguration` fields (each with a `MODEL_CONFIGURATION_VALIDATOR` entry), following the same pattern used to bake in `allowImportChanges` and `supportsNextCursorLinePrediction`.
- Every read site resolves via `modelConfig.<field> ?? experimentDefault`, so behavior is unchanged for any strategy that does not set a value.
- `selectedModelConfiguration()` returns the strategy-resolved config, so consumers outside `xtabProvider` observe the baked values:
  - **xtabProvider** (`patchModelPredictionKind`, `splitPatchOnDiff`, `patchFastYieldLineWithCursor`, `extraDebounceEndOfLine`) via the already-resolved model config.
  - **NextEditProvider** (`cacheDelay`, `rebasedCacheDelay`) and **UserInteractionMonitor** (`debounce`) inject `IInlineEditsModelService`.
  - **inline completion provider** (`nesMimicGhostTextBehavior`) via its existing model service.
- Adds a reusable `NullInlineEditsModelService` test double for the newly-injected dependency.

### Completions unification

`supportsUnifiedCompletions` bakes completions unification into the strategy, following the exact `supportsNextCursorLinePrediction` precedent where a baked capability overrides the deployment toggle at each read site. When the selected NES model's strategy sets it, the client runs as the single unified provider — one baked boolean replaces all three unification settings:

- **`inlineCompletionProvider.ts`**: `unification` resolves via `selectedModelConfiguration().supportsUnifiedCompletions ?? InlineEditsUnification` (replaces `github.copilot.chat.advanced.inlineEdits.unification`).
- **`jointInlineCompletionProvider.ts`**: the baked flag is observed reactively (via `onModelListUpdated`) and OR-ed into the effective `modelUnification`, which both suppresses the separate GitHub Copilot completions provider and pushes `github.copilot` into the provider `excludes` (replaces `inlineCompletionsUnificationModel` (ExP) and `excludedProviders: "completions,github.copilot"` (local)).

The baked value never replaces the existing experiment path for other models — it only short-circuits it when set, so unrelated deployments are unaffected.

### Intended deployment

```jsonc
{
  "modelConfiguration": {
    "modelName": "copilot-suggestions-lysithea-0024",
    "promptingStrategy": "patchBased02Optimized",
    "includeTagsInCurrentFile": false
  }
}
```

No `inlineCompletionsUnificationModel` / `unification` / `excludedProviders` toggles are required — the strategy carries them.

## Testing

- `npm run typecheck --prefix extensions/copilot`
- focused Vitest coverage for `applyStrategyConfig`, `MODEL_CONFIGURATION_VALIDATOR`, `pickSystemPrompt`, `NextEditProvider` caching/speculative, and `UserInteractionMonitor`
- `npm run precommit`

body:
The responsive single-pane layout may automatically hide the auxiliary bar when the Agents Window becomes too narrow. When the window later becomes wider, the auxiliary bar should **not** automatically reopen. Reopening should require explicit user intent.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Open a workspace session in the Agents Window using the single-pane layout.
2. Show the auxiliary bar/Details area.
3. Resize the window narrower until responsive layout hides the auxiliary bar.
4. Resize the window wider again without interacting with the side-pane sash or layout actions.

## Expected

- The auxiliary bar remains hidden when the window becomes wider.
- The responsive layout does not infer that more width means the user wants the auxiliary bar reopened.
- The user can reopen it explicitly by dragging the side-pane sash or invoking the appropriate show/toggle action.

## Actual

The auxiliary bar can automatically reopen as the window becomes wider, overriding the current hidden layout state.

## Rationale

Responsive behavior should be asymmetric: it may remove UI when space becomes constrained, but it should not restore UI without explicit user intent. This avoids layout jumps while resizing the window.

Related: #330409 tracked a different intermittent narrow-pane symptom and was closed after more information was not provided.

body: ## Feature Request: Add a minimize/collapse action for long-running progress notifications ### Description VS Code displays a persistent progress notification for long-running operations such as: > Opening Java Projects: check details When the operation takes a significant amount of time, this notification remains visible and cannot be dismissed or minimized while the operation continues. This can obstruct part of the editor and become distracting, especially when working with large Java/Maven projects where project initialization or indexing may take several minutes. ### Expected behavior Long-running progress notifications should provide an option to **minimize/collapse the notification** while allowing the underlying operation to continue. For example: * **Minimize/Collapse** → hides the notification from the editor area and moves the progress indication to the status bar. * The user can later expand the notification to check its progress/details. * The operation should continue normally in the background. ### Current behavior The notification remains visible while the operation is running, with no obvious way to minimize it. For example: `Opening Java Projects: check details` The notification can only disappear once the underlying operation finishes. ### Use case This is particularly noticeable with the Java extension when opening large or multi-module Maven projects. Java project initialization can take several minutes, during which the progress notification remains on screen. A similar minimize-to-status-bar behavior already exists for some long-running operations, so applying the same UX pattern to other persistent progress notifications would make the experience less intrusive. ### Suggested UI Add a **Minimize/Collapse** button to persistent progress notifications. When minimized: `Opening Java Projects... [progress]` could become a compact status-bar progress indicator or disappear into notification icon, while the user can continue using the editor without the notification taking up screen space. ### Screenshot The attached screenshot shows the `Opening Java Projects: check details` notification remaining visible during Java project initialization. ### Environment * VS Code: 1.134.0 * OS: Ubuntu/Linux * Java project using Maven * Java extension / Extension Pack for Java ### Related issue This is related to the Java extension issue concerning the long-running `Opening Java Projects: check details` progress notification: #2643. However, this request is specifically about **providing a way to minimize/collapse the progress notification**, rather than improving the Java project import performance.

title: [cherry-pick] chat: don't prompt for workspace trust on internal agent-session folders

labels.name: cherry-pick-artifact
labels.description: Auto-generated cherry-pick PR

body:
Cherry-pick of #332280 from `release/1.135`.

Fixes #332249

## Problem

The send-time workspace-trust gate added for agent-host chat treated two **internal** folders as user workspaces and prompted _"Do you trust the authors of the files in this folder?"_:

1. **Workspace-less quick chats** — the agent host runs them in an internal scratch dir `~/.copilot/chats/<id>`, which is persisted as the session's working directory. The gate read `workingDirectories` but ignored the `workspaceless` marker, so it prompted for the scratch dir.
2. **Worktree sessions** — VS Code creates isolated worktrees in a **sibling** `<repo>.worktrees/<name>` dir. Workspace-trust inheritance is equal-or-descendant only, so trusting `/repo` does not cover `/repo.worktrees/x`; opening such a session from the list (and a follow-up send) prompted even though the base repo is trusted.

Regression from #331895 / #331981.

## Fix

- **Quick chats:** `AgentHostSessionHandler._resolveSessionTrustFolders` now reads the session state once and, when `readSessionWorkspaceless(state._meta)` is set, returns a sentinel so `_invokeAgent` **skips the folder-trust gate** entirely — the scratch dir is an implementation detail, not a user workspace.
- **Worktrees:** trust is **inherited from the already-trusted base repository** before the gates run:
  - `SessionsService.canOpenSession` calls a shared `ensureSessionWorktreesTrusted` helper (open gate).
  - The handler's send gate applies the equivalent inheritance (covers follow-up turns, which bypass the sessions open gate — the handler is the only universal chokepoint).
  - Both are guarded **structurally** to `getWorktreesRoot(<repo>)`: bare `workTreeUri` does not prove VS Code created the worktree, so a working directory outside `<repo>.worktrees` can never inherit trust just because its reported base repo is trusted (addresses the [#331981 review note](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/331981#discussion_r3831310974)).
- Extracts `getWorktreesRoot` into `platform/agentHost/common/worktreePaths.ts` so the node agent host and the browser trust gates share one implementation.

## Validation

- `npm run typecheck-client` — clean; `npm run valid-layers-check` — passed.
- Browser unit tests: `workspaceFolderManagement` (8) and agent-host `workspace trust` suite (10, incl. 5 new: quick-chat skip, worktree grant + follow-up turn, untrusted-repo prompt, structural-guard rejection, worktree-pending window).
- Full node unit suite: 15198 passing, 0 failing.

## Manual testing

- **Quick chat:** clear trust → Agents Window → "New Quick Chat" → send → no trust dialog (previously prompted for `~/.copilot/chats/<id>`). Control: "New Session" on an untrusted folder still prompts.
- **Worktree:** trust only a base repo → "New Session" on it with Worktree isolation → send (creates `<repo>.worktrees/<name>`) → reload → open from list and send a follow-up → no prompt. Control: with the base repo untrusted, it still prompts.

## Notes

- Branch is based on `release/1.135` (the regression ships in 1.135), so this PR targets `release/1.135`.
- Deferred follow-ups: validating creation provenance via `WORKTREE_META_REPOSITORY_ROOT` (stronger than the structural guard), and worktree-trust lifecycle/revocation (pre-existing; `setUrisTrust` is never revoked on worktree deletion).

title: File links use Windows paths in non-Local multi-root sessions on Remote WSL
body:
- Copilot Chat Extension Version: 0.62.0 (bundled)
- VS Code Version: 1.134.0 (`110a328ea54b42367b803ec53ee0bf52ef26b419`)
- Remote - WSL Extension Version: 0.104.3
- OS Version: Windows 10.0.26200.9106; WSL 2.7.12.0; Ubuntu; Linux kernel 6.18.33.2-microsoft-standard-WSL2
- Feature: File links in session chat responses in a Remote - WSL multi-root workspace
- Selected model: Model-independent; VS Code renders and opens the links

File links produced in a multi-root session that is not Local are converted to Windows-style paths and do not open in a Remote - WSL window. The same kind of link produced in a multi-root session delegated to Local retains forward slashes and opens successfully.

I have not tested single-root sessions, so this report makes no claim about their behavior.

The experimental `chat.agentHost.copilotAgent.multiRootEnabled` setting was enabled because a multi-root session can be delegated to Local only if the setting was already enabled when that session was created. To test the Local behavior, I therefore created a new eligible multi-root session and delegated it to Local, and that solves the problem for new sessions.

Steps to Reproduce / Observed Comparison:

1. Open a multi-root workspace in a Remote - WSL window.
2. In a multi-root session that is not Local, ask the agent to create a file such as `/tmp/example.log` and provide a link to it, or to link an existing workspace file such as `/home/user/project/src/example.ts`.
3. Hover the link. VS Code displays the POSIX path with Windows-style backslashes, for example `\tmp\example.log` or `\home\user\project\src\example.ts`.
4. Click the link. The editor reports that the file was not found and does not open it.
5. For comparison, ensure `chat.agentHost.copilotAgent.multiRootEnabled` is enabled before creating another multi-root session.
6. Create the new multi-root session and delegate it to Local.
7. Repeat the same request in the Local multi-root session.
8. The Local session's link displays forward slashes and opens successfully.

The files exist and open normally from the WSL Explorer or **File > Open File** in both cases.

For the affected non-Local multi-root session, manually providing an explicit remote URI also fails:

```markdown
[example.ts](vscode-remote://wsl+ubuntu/home/user/project/src/example.ts)
```

VS Code serializes the authority as `wsl%2Bubuntu`, then attempts to resolve that URI without a matching filesystem provider. The renderer log records:

```text
[RemoteAgentHostProtocol] Request failed: Resource not found: vscode-remote://wsl%2Bubuntu/home/user/project/src/example.ts
[RemoteAgentHostProtocol] Request failed: Failed to read content: vscode-remote://wsl%2Bubuntu/home/user/project/src/example.ts: ENOPRO: No file system provider found for resource 'vscode-remote://wsl%2Bubuntu/home/user/project/src/example.ts'
Error: The editor could not be opened because the file was not found.
```

Expected:

File links in both Local and non-Local multi-root sessions preserve POSIX separators and open through the current WSL remote filesystem.

Actual:

- Non-Local multi-root session links are displayed as Windows paths and cannot open WSL files.
- Local multi-root session links retain forward slashes and open successfully.
- The broken behavior affects files both inside workspace roots and elsewhere in the WSL filesystem, including `/tmp`.
- Single-root sessions were not tested.

Note about the experimental setting:

`chat.agentHost.copilotAgent.multiRootEnabled` must be enabled before a multi-root session is created for that session to be eligible for delegation to Local. This eligibility requirement is separate from the file-link bug.

Related:

- #293492
- #251076
- #301167

Opening a markdown file with the "Open as Preview" button leaves the preview without keyboard focus, so Find cannot be opened from the keyboard until the preview is clicked. The Edit > Find menu item never opens the Find widget at all, whether or not the preview has been clicked.

Steps to Reproduce:

title: agent host: normalize empty Kerberos proxy SPN to avoid spurious restart
body:
Fixes #332305
Fixes https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-internalbacklog/issues/8895
For https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/331648

## Problem

Restarting VS Code with an Agents Window session sometimes leaves the **Chat Panel empty** ("Couldn't open session"), even though the session data is intact. This is a spurious Copilot SDK client restart that tears down a healthy client **mid session-restore**.

The trigger is the Kerberos proxy SPN (`http.proxyKerberosServicePrincipal`), which reaches the agent host as two different representations of the same "not configured" state:

- When the Copilot client first spawns (on the reconnect-after-restart path), the host reads the setting as **absent** → `undefined` and records that as the applied baseline (`_applyProxyEnv`).
- A moment later the workbench mirrors its config down. The mirror transform coerces an **unset** setting to an **empty string** (`request.ts`: `value => typeof value === 'string' ? value : ''`). The `''` is load-bearing — it is how *clearing* a previously-set SPN propagates under the host's **merge** reducer, so it cannot simply be dropped.

`_refreshProxy` then compared the two values raw:

```
'' === undefined  →  false  →  "proxy config changed"  →  restart the Copilot client
```

Because the restart is not deferred during a restore, it calls `_stopClient()`, the in-flight resume's `_throwIfClientReplaced` throws a `CancellationError` ("Canceled"), that error is not classified as recoverable and the resume is not retried — so the panel is left empty. It is a race (spawn must win over the config push), which is why it only reproduces intermittently and only after a restart. The misleading `CAPI proxy configuration changed ((none) -> (none))` log hid that the SPN — not the proxy URL — drove the restart.

Only the SPN is affected: the proxy URL and no-proxy list are normalized before the restart comparison, and the sibling `enterpriseHost` already collapses empty≡absent (`enterpriseUri || undefined`). The SPN was the one proxy key compared raw.

## Fix

Read the SPN through a single helper, `_readKerberosSpn`, that normalizes `''` to `undefined`, and use it at **both** read sites — the applied baseline (`_applyProxyEnv`) and the effective value (`_refreshProxy`). Now an absent-vs-empty transition compares `undefined === undefined` and no restart is requested. This mirrors the existing `enterpriseHost` normalization and matches how the SPN is already treated everywhere it is *used* (the Kerberos lookup falls back to a hostname default for any falsy SPN), so it is a semantic reconciliation rather than a workaround.

Also replaced the misleading restart log with one that names the actual trigger(s) (`proxy … -> …` and/or `Kerberos SPN changed`).

### Why the fix lives on the host, not the workbench transform
Making the transform emit `undefined` would regress clearing a set SPN: the patch builder omits `undefined` keys and the host reducer *merges* patches, so the old value would survive. The reconciliation belongs on the host.

## Tests

Added two regression tests to the `restart on startup config change` suite in `copilotAgent.test.ts`:

- **`does not restart the Copilot runtime when an unset Kerberos proxy SPN is mirrored as empty`** — the core regression. Verified **red before / green after**: without the fix it fails with `stopCallCount: 1` (spurious restart); with the fix `startCallCount: 1, stopCallCount: 0` and the proxy refresh still runs.
- **`restarts the Copilot runtime without a Kerberos proxy SPN when a configured SPN is cleared`** — a guard proving the normalization does **not** suppress a legitimate clear (`A → ""` still restarts and respawns without the SPN).

All 5 Kerberos SPN tests pass. `tsc --noEmit` and ESLint are clean.

title: chat: Refresh customization source after harness registration
body:
I generated this by scanning my logs, pls take if it's good/useful

---
🤖 

## Summary

- cache an empty AI customization item source while its harness descriptor is unavailable
- invalidate that cache when the matching descriptor is registered or replaced
- refresh already-observed customization sections after late harness registration

## Problem

Recent Insiders renderer logs repeatedly emitted warnings during startup while customization harnesses were still registering:

```text
2026-08-17 15:21:43.525 [warning] No harness descriptor found for session type file
2026-08-17 15:21:43.783 [warning] No harness descriptor found for session type agent-host-copilotcli
```

The same warning appeared in bursts because `AICustomizationItemsModel` deliberately did not reuse `EmptyItemProviderItemSource`. Each access before harness registration therefore constructed and disposed another empty source and logged again.

The model also did not observe harness registration as an input to its source cache. As a result, an already-observed section could remain bound to the placeholder source until another unrelated change caused the source to be rebuilt.

## Fix

Keep the existing `MutableDisposable` source cache and make its cache identity include both:

- the active session resource
- the resolved harness descriptor identity

The existing autorun now resolves the descriptor from the observed `availableHarnesses` value and passes it to the cache. This means:

- repeated reads while the descriptor is missing reuse one empty source
- registering the descriptor changes cache identity, replaces the placeholder source, and refetches observed sections
- re-registering a descriptor under the same ID still creates a fresh source

The change intentionally preserves the existing cache and lifecycle structure rather than introducing a broader observable refactor.

## Tests

Added a regression test that verifies the placeholder source is reused, then replaced and fetched exactly once when its harness registers.

- `npm run typecheck-client`
- `./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/aiCustomization/aiCustomizationItemsModel.test.ts` — 30 passing
- pre-commit hygiene — passed

title: fix(markdown): preserve table delimiter rows when injecting diff markers (closes #332119)
body: ## Summary Prevents Markdown diff inner change markers (`` / ``) from being injected into structural delimiter lines (such as table delimiter rows, code block fences, and horizontal rules), ensuring Markdown tables and code blocks parse correctly in visual diff previews. ## Problem When reviewing changes to a Markdown file containing a table in the Source Control rendered Markdown diff preview: 1. If a cell edit causes a column width change (or if a formatter re-aligns table pipes), the git diff detects changes across table delimiter rows (e.g. `| --- | --- |`). 2. The inner change diff injector places `` / `` marker tags into the table delimiter row. 3. Because the delimiter row no longer consists strictly of pipes, dashes, colons, and whitespace, markdown-it's GFM table parser fails to recognize the table syntax. 4. The entire table collapses into a block of raw unformatted text with literal pipes and dashes, making the diff unreadable. ## Root Cause `injectInnerChangeMarkers` in `documentRenderer.ts` injected diff marker `` tags into all modified lines without checking whether a line represents a Markdown structural block delimiter. When tags were inserted into table delimiter rows (e.g. `| --- |`), the delimiter row ceased to satisfy GFM table grammar rules. ## Solution 1. Added `isStructuralDelimiterLine` helper to `documentRenderer.ts` to identify structural Markdown lines: - Table delimiter rows (e.g. `| --- | :---: | ---: |` or `|---|---|`). - Code block fences (```` ``` ```` or `~~~`). - Thematic breaks / horizontal rules / frontmatter delimiters (`---`, `===`, `***`, `___`). 2. Skipped inner change marker tag injection for structural delimiter lines in `injectInnerChangeMarkers`. 3. Table headers and table body cells continue to receive inner change markers for rich in-cell word diff highlights, while the delimiter row remains clean so markdown-it renders an HTML ``. 4. Added test coverage in `engine.test.ts`. ## Behavioral Changes - Before: Editing table columns or reformatting table delimiter rows turned the rendered Markdown diff into raw unformatted pipes and dashes. - After: The table delimiter row remains valid GFM syntax, allowing the table to render as an HTML table with highlighted cell edits. ## Testing - Ran `node --experimental-strip-types build/hygiene.ts` (passed with 0 errors). - Ran `node --experimental-strip-types build/checker/layersChecker.ts` (passed with 0 errors). - Added regression test in `engine.test.ts`. ## Edge Cases Considered - Multi-column tables with varying alignment colons (`:---`, `:---:`, `---:`). - Compact tables without leading/trailing pipes (e.g. `Col A | Col B\n---|---`). - Tables inside blockquotes or indented contexts. - Genuine content lines containing single hyphens (e.g. `| - | text |`): only lines where every cell is a delimiter are recognized as structural. ## Compatibility - Backwards-compatible; preserves all existing diff highlighting for non-delimiter lines and cell content. ## Related Issue Closes #332119

title: chat: keep an agent turn's changes summary from flickering
body:
## What

The per-turn **"N files changed +A -B"** summary under a completed agent turn in the Agents window appeared, disappeared, reappeared, and sometimes stayed hidden for good.

## Why it happened

Every source behind the summary has windows where it legitimately reports no files, and `AgentHostResponseFileChangesProvider` treated each of them as *"this turn changed nothing"* — which makes each consumer hide itself:

- The part renders before session state resolves, so there is no turn changeset URI yet.
- Subscribing triggers `computeTurnChangeset`, whose `registerChangeset` seeds `{ status: Computing, files: [] }`.
- `onTurnComplete` schedules a **second** recompute for the same turn, flipping the status back to `Computing`. The old code required `status === Ready`, so it threw away files it already had (the reducer deliberately preserves `files` across a status change) and fell back to the response stream — which is empty while the turn moves from `activeTurn` to `turns`. That is the second flicker.
- A failed compute (`ChangesetStatus.Error`), an evicted changeset state, or a genuinely empty git turn diff left the summary hidden permanently.

The subscription is also released whenever the derived loses all observers (list recycling, the part being recreated when `isLastTurn` flips), so every re-read restarts from an empty snapshot.

## What changed

**`agentHostResponseFileChanges.ts`** — per-request diffs are now monotonic:

- Non-empty changeset files win regardless of status, so a recompute or an error keeps the last published list instead of falling back.
- An empty `Ready` changeset is still authoritative ("this turn changed nothing"), but only before anything has been shown — so no-op turns stay hidden and never appear-then-vanish.
- Otherwise the response stream, otherwise the previously emitted value.

**`chatTurnPillsPart.ts`** — the part latches its diffs as well, covering what the provider latch cannot: the observable being rebuilt on reconnect, LRU eviction, or the part being recreated.

**Logging** — each turn traces its diff source on change:

```
[AgentHostResponseFileChanges] <session> turn <id>: diffs from 'changeset|response|retained|authoritativeEmpty|unsupported' (files=N, changesetStatus=…)
```

## Reviewer notes

- **Trade-off:** a turn that shows streamed file-edit counts and whose authoritative changeset then computes to zero files now keeps the streamed counts instead of hiding. A trace line with `source='response'`/`'retained'` **and** `changesetStatus=ready` identifies exactly that case.
- `AgentHostResponseFileChangesProvider` gained a required `ILogService` parameter; `_resolveBackendChat` is now explicitly `| undefined` since it precedes it.
- `ChatCheckpointFileChangesSummaryContentPart` is untouched — it consumes the same provider, so agent-host sessions get the fix there too, while local chat sessions keep their existing behavior.

## Validation

- New provider test walks `Ready → Computing → Error → session-state loss → Ready-empty` and asserts the counts never change.
- New `ChatTurnPillsContentPart` test asserts the summary stays visible after its diffs go empty.
- `scripts\test.bat` over the provider, turn pills and checkpoint summary suites: 15 passing. `npm run typecheck-client` clean, eslint clean on changed files.

title: fix(mermaid): strip diff markers from diagram source before parsing (closes #332107)
body: ## Summary Strips injected visual diff markers (`` / ``) from Mermaid diagram sources before diagram parsing and rendering in Markdown previews, notebooks, and webviews. ## Problem When reviewing changes to a Markdown file containing Mermaid diagrams in the Source Control rendered Markdown diff preview: 1. The diff preview engine injects inner change marker tags (`` and ``) into modified lines. 2. For fenced Mermaid blocks, the marker tags are preserved in the container element's text content. 3. Mermaid's parser fails with syntax parse errors (such as `Parse error on line 3: ...||--o{ TEAM: "have"` and `` into raw Markdown lines to enable CSS Custom Highlight API ranges. 2. In `mermaid-markdown-features`, `renderMermaidElement` extracts `(mermaidContainer.textContent ?? '').trim()`. Because `textContent` automatically unescapes the HTML entities produced by markdown-it, the raw diagram source string contains literal `` tags. 3. Mermaid's grammar parser (`mermaid.parse()` and `mermaid.render()`) does not permit HTML `` tags within diagram declarations, leading to an immediate parse exception. ## Solution 1. Added `stripDiffMarkers` in `extensions/mermaid-markdown-features/preview-src/shared/index.ts` to strip `` and `` tags from diagram source text before parsing and rendering. 2. Applied `stripDiffMarkers` in `renderMermaidElement` (`shared/index.ts`) and `initializeMermaidWebview` (`chat/mermaidWebview.ts`). 3. Preserved all legitimate Mermaid parsing error reporting when user diagram source contains actual syntax errors. ## Behavioral Changes - Before: Editing lines inside a Mermaid code block caused the rendered Markdown diff preview to crash with a Mermaid syntax parse error containing `` tags. - After: Diff markers are stripped from the diagram source passed to Mermaid, allowing the diagram to compile and render as expected in diff views while retaining standard error diagnostics for genuine syntax errors. ## Testing - Ran `node --experimental-strip-types build/hygiene.ts` (passed with 0 errors). - Ran `node --experimental-strip-types build/checker/layersChecker.ts` (passed with 0 errors). - Verified `stripDiffMarkers` handles single/multiple markers, single and double quote attribute formats, and whitespace variations without altering user diagram text or custom node labels. ## Edge Cases Considered - Empty diagram blocks. - Multiple diff markers across different lines in a single diagram. - Legitimate HTML/brackets inside Mermaid node labels (e.g. `A["Label <1>"]`): only tags with `data-diff-(start|end)` attributes are removed; user brackets are preserved. - Syntax errors in user diagrams: real errors continue to be caught and formatted with `createMermaidErrorElement`. ## Compatibility - Backwards-compatible; only strips internal VS Code diff marker tags during diagram compilation. ## Related Issue Closes #332107

## SDK/CLI bump — automated integration fix

**Bump:** `@github/copilot-sdk@1.0.12-preview.0` + CLI `1.0.81-8` · base `main` · fix cycle **4**

### This cycle — escalation: upstream runtime history-projection regression



Product build **467354** failed **5 Agent Host E2E integration tests, all in the Copilot suite** (Conformance, Claude, and Codex suites all pass). Every failure is the same class: **prior conversation history / error state does not survive reconstruction** (fork, side-chat, host-restart, subagent-reopen), even though VS Code's own visible turns (`chatState().turns` / `seededMessages`) are correct.

| # | Test | Symptom |
|---|------|---------|
| 1 | `subagentSuite.ts:219` — reopening a session keeps sub-agent messages out of the parent transcript (replay path) | reopened parent's `responsePartIds` identical to live; parent not reconstructed from persisted provider state |
| 2 | `multiChatSuite.ts:478` (test `forked peer chat inherits source history`) | `requestHasPriorUserMessage`/`requestHasPriorAssistantMessage` are `false`; visible fork history present but not reaching the model request |
| 3/4 | side-chat `[capi-replay]` request #2 (after-each `agentHostE2ESuites.js:119`) | recorded fixture has prior user+assistant turns before the side-chat-context message; live request has ONLY the side-chat-context message — history dropped |
| 5 | Copilot `request error survives a host restart` | after restart, live now produces full nested `error._meta.chatError.fetchError.capiError` + `errorType:"query"` + `state:"error"`; fixture predates this — error state now *survives* restart |

### Root cause — runtime-owned, not a VS Code integration gap

Independent read-through of every VS Code integration surface confirms they are **correct and unchanged** from prior green builds:

- **Fork provisioning** (`copilotAgent.ts::_forkSdkChat`): resolves `getForkBoundaryEventId(turnId)` (exclusive `toEventId`), calls `client.rpc.sessions.fork`, VACUUMs source DB into target. For single-turn fork, `getNextTurnEventId` returns `undefined` → fork includes **all** events. Correct.
- **Fork boundary** (`copilotAgentSession.ts::getForkBoundaryEventId`, `truncateAtEventId`, `getNextTurnEventId`/`getFirstTurnEventId`): unchanged, correct. Turn event-ids recorded via `setTurnEventId(turnId, e.id)` on `onUserMessage` — unchanged.
- **Resume config** (`copilotSessionLauncher.ts::launch`/`resumeSession`): no new/missing resume option; SDK `SessionsForkRequest` (`sessionId`, `toEventId?`, `name?`) is **unchanged** — no new history-replay knob exists to pass.
- **Reconstruction** (`mapSessionEvents.ts`, `buildSessionEvents.ts`): SDK event shapes standard/unchanged; message/tool arms fold correctly.

The failures span **4 distinct reconstruction mechanisms simultaneously**, and #2/#3/#4 compare **live** model requests (genuine dropped history, not fixture staleness) — so re-recording fixtures would **mask a real regression** and is not done. The runtime resume path (`registry.rs::hydrate_from_events` / `begin_hydrate_from_events`, `event_projection.rs`) is where persisted/forked events are folded into the model request on resume, and that surface is runtime-owned.

### SDK+CLI correlation

Combined SDK + CLI bump (SDK `1.0.12-preview.0`, CLI `1.0.81-8`). Slack canary threads are all `1.0.12-canary.*` + `1.0.81-canary.*.unsigned` (different unsigned builds) and have failed **persistently across the entire 1.0.12/1.0.81 canary line** with the same reconstruction-history-drop signatures — corroborating a real upstream issue in this line, not a VS Code integration gap. The authoritative signed-pair product build (467354) reproduces the identical failures.

### Why escalate now (cycle 4, under the cap)

Cycle 3 already suspected this upstream and permitted another build; build 467354 reproduced the **same class**, now broader (4 reconstruction paths). No VS Code-side edit can fix this without fabricating/re-seeding the lost history into the model request, which would mask a genuine runtime regression (explicitly discouraged). No version pins or lockfiles touched; `extensions/copilot` left frozen; no packaging/signing/network changes. Handing to the VS Code reviewers for an upstream SDK/CLI fix rather than burning cycle 5 on a masking workaround.

### Product-build state

Build 467354 failed (5 Copilot Agent Host E2E reconstruction tests). No code pushed this cycle — escalated as an upstream runtime history-projection regression.
